title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom  on 1968-03-29
lineage: AUD > MR > D > PCM > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Phenomenal audience tape from ’68 with crisp Dark Star and a high‑energy four‑song set featuring Sittin’ On Top Of The World and Death Don't Have No Mercy.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience capture that sounds astonishingly clear for 1968, delivering a crisp Dark Star and surprisingly clean ambience. Musically the brief four‑track set is a highlight of the year, resurrecting rare early versions of Sittin’ On Top Of The World, Death Don’t Have No Mercy and a deep‑throated Garcia vocal that fans rave about. While a few reviewers note minor tape quirks and misdating, the overall performance and sound quality are praised as exceptional for an old audience cassette.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈80%) award 5‑star ratings, praising both the musical performance and the surprisingly high sound quality; only a few modest critiques lower the average slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with minimal audience noise; reviewers note it sounds phenomenal for a 1968 audience cassette despite occasional minor flaws (echo differences, tiny drop‑outs).

standout_songs: Sittin' On Top Of The World
show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise four‑song set that captures the high‑energy early‑68 vibe, featuring resurrected 1966 material and an early truncated Dark Star; the flow is tight despite its brevity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s deep‑throated vocals and expressive guitar work are highlighted as strong points throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s spoken quip after Sittin’ On Top is noted (some think it sounds like Phil rather than Jerry) and his comment about never doing the song well is quoted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Simple keyboard accompaniment is mentioned, noting the stripped‑down sound typical of early ’68.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s presence is emphasized (many assume only Bill was playing); reviewers point out the single‑drummer feel but confirm Mickey was in the band at this time.
